\begin{theorem}[A binomial power inequality]
\lean{FABL.two_mul_delta_mul_card_mul_pow_le_one_sub_pow}
\label{FABL.two_mul_delta_mul_card_mul_pow_le_one_sub_pow}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
For every real number $\delta$ with $0\leq\delta\leq\tfrac12$ and every natural number
$k$,
\[2\delta k(1-2\delta)^{k-1}\leq 1-(1-2\delta)^k.\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Stable influence bounded by noise sensitivity]
\lean{FABL.delta_mul_totalStableInfluence_le_noiseSensitivity}
\label{FABL.delta_mul_totalStableInfluence_le_noiseSensitivity}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.noiseSensitivity, FABL.totalStableInfluence, FABL.totalStableInfluence_eq_sum_card_mul_rho_pow_mul_sq_fourierCoeff, FABL.two_mul_delta_mul_card_mul_pow_le_one_sub_pow, FABL.two_mul_noiseSensitivity_eq_sum_fourier}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$, and let $\delta\in\mathbb{R}$
satisfy $0<\delta$ and $\delta\le\tfrac12$. Then $\delta$ times the total stable
influence of the real-valued sign version of $f$, at correlation $1-2\delta$, is at most
the noise sensitivity of $f$ at noise rate $\delta$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Noise sensitivity derivative bound]
\lean{FABL.deriv_noiseSensitivityCurve_le_sqrt_three_halves_div_sqrt_of_isLinearThreshold}
\label{FABL.deriv_noiseSensitivityCurve_le_sqrt_three_halves_div_sqrt_of_isLinearThreshold}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.IsLinearThreshold, FABL.PositiveHalfNoiseParameter, FABL.delta_mul_totalStableInfluence_le_noiseSensitivity, FABL.hasDerivAt_noiseSensitivityCurve, FABL.noiseSensitivityCurve, FABL.peresNoiseSensitivityBound, FABL.totalStableInfluence}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be a linear threshold function: there are real weights
$a_0,a_1,\ldots,a_n$ such that $f(x)$ is the sign of $a_0+\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i$, with
zero assigned the positive sign. For $0<\delta\le 1/2$, let
$N_f(\delta)=\bigl(1-\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}(1-2\delta)^{|S|}\widehat f(S)^2\bigr)/2$,
where $\widehat f(S)$ are the uniform Fourier coefficients of $f$. Then $N_f'(\delta)\le
\sqrt{3/2}/\sqrt{\delta}$.
\end{theorem}
